question: What does social inclusion mean for a person living with a physical disability?

options.A: Depending entirely on family members for all daily social interactions
options.B: Living exclusively in specialized care facilities with other disabled peers
options.C: Having equal opportunities to work, learn, and participate in community life
options.D: Avoiding public spaces to prevent unwanted attention from strangers

explanation: Social inclusion ensures full participation in society, including employment, education, voting, and recreation. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h8)

question: What is a key difference between the anterior and posterior pituitary lobes?

options.A: The anterior lobe releases oxytocin into the bloodstream.
options.B: The anterior lobe ignores signals from the hypothalamus.
options.C: The posterior lobe produces growth hormone directly.
options.D: The posterior lobe only stores hormones made by the hypothalamus.

explanation: Well done! Think of the posterior pituitary as a warehouse—it doesn't make oxytocin or ADH itself, it just stores and releases them. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is a simulation laboratory considered a safe learning space for nursing students?

options.A: Instructors are not allowed to point out mistakes
options.B: Students are never evaluated on their performance
options.C: There is no pressure or stress during the exercises
options.D: Errors made during scenarios do not harm real patients

explanation: Because mannequins or actors are used instead of real people, students can make and learn from mistakes safely. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why is contact tracing such an important tool for managing contagious diseases?

options.A: It eliminates the need for environmental testing in public water
options.B: It automatically cures patients who were exposed to the germ
options.C: It allows nurses to identify, test, and isolate exposed individuals early
options.D: It turns healthy carriers into clinical cases

explanation: Contact tracing helps us track down people who might have been exposed, letting us isolate and care for them before the virus spreads further. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h5)

question: A nursing lecturer wants students to practice breaking bad news to a worried family member. Which method fits this best?

options.A: A standard lecture
options.B: Silent independent reading
options.C: Memorizing drug dosages
options.D: Role-playing

explanation: Role-play is brilliant for building communication and soft skills in a safe space before you ever have to face that situation with a real patient. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h3)

question: What was the big shift in thinking brought by the Ottawa Charter?

options.A: Transferring all health responsibilities from governments to private individuals
options.B: Mandating that every village must build a modern tertiary hospital
options.C: Focusing exclusively on pharmaceutical distribution in developing nations
options.D: Shifting focus away from just treating sickness toward social and environmental living conditions

explanation: You've got this! The Charter expanded our understanding of health beyond just hospitals and doctors to include living conditions, policies, and community environments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important to document the exact number of shocks the AED delivered during a code?

options.A: It tells the biomedical department when to throw away the machine's battery.
options.B: It provides critical data for the medical team reviewing the patient's clinical course.
options.C: It proves to the hospital administration that the nurse followed the correct protocol.
options.D: It determines how much financial charge the patient receives for equipment use.

explanation: Doctors and the healthcare team need to know how many shocks were given to understand how the patient's heart responded and plan their next steps. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h7)

question: Which group of psychiatric drugs is most famous for causing rapid weight gain?

options.A: Short-acting sleeping tablets
options.B: Standard over-the-counter vitamins
options.C: Mild herbal anxiety supplements
options.D: Second-generation antipsychotics

explanation: Correct! These medications heavily impact metabolism and appetite control, often leading to rapid weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: What does intersectoral collaboration mean in community health practice?

options.A: Transferring all sick patients directly to tertiary teaching hospitals without delay
options.B: Working together with non-health sectors like agriculture and education to improve health
options.C: Merging all community health clinics under one central government ministry
options.D: Requiring nurses to perform the duties of doctors and pharmacists simultaneously

explanation: Intersectoral collaboration involves partnering with different sectors outside health because social determinants of health span multiple fields. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h7)

question: Which method is commonly used by nurse managers to evaluate if nursing documentation standards are being met?

options.A: Pharmacy stock counts
options.B: Patient dietary reviews
options.C: Chart audits
options.D: Staff fashion shows

explanation: Reviewing patient clinical records allows managers to see if charting and care standards are being followed accurately. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: Which chemical is mainly responsible for opening up blood vessels during inflammation?

options.A: Pepsin
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Insulin

explanation: When tissues get hurt, mast cells release histamine. This chemical widens local blood vessels so helpful immune cells can rush to the rescue. [learn more](GST114_U4_T4#GST114_U4_T4_h4)

question: What simple instruction should a nurse give a patient after they use a corticosteroid inhaler?

options.A: Rinse the mouth thoroughly with water and spit it out
options.B: Eat a small snack immediately to protect the throat lining
options.C: Brush the teeth firmly with a hard-bristled toothbrush
options.D: Drink a full glass of milk to neutralize remaining residue

explanation: Always remind patients to rinse and spit! Getting leftover steroid out of the mouth prevents nasty fungal infections like thrush and throat hoarseness. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why do we use barium sulfate during a barium meal X-ray test?

options.A: To act as a contrast medium on X-rays
options.B: To neutralize excess stomach acid
options.C: To numb the lining of the stomach
options.D: To speed up the digestion of food

explanation: You're doing great! Barium coats the inside of the gut and blocks X-rays so we can see the organs clearly on the screen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h1)

question: What is the name of the temperature zone where bacteria grow and multiply the fastest?

options.C: 0°C to 4°C
options.D: 5°C to 60°C

explanation: The 'danger zone' is between 5°C and 60°C. In this warmth, bacteria can double in number in just twenty minutes! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h5)

question: How does a 'just culture' respond when a nurse makes an honest, accidental error?

options.A: It requires the nurse to pay out-of-pocket for any hospital damages
options.B: It mandates immediate termination of employment to protect patients
options.C: It treats the error as a signal to examine and fix the underlying system
options.D: It ignores the incident completely to avoid creating paperwork

explanation: A just culture knows good nurses make mistakes. Instead of pointing fingers, it asks: 'How can we fix the system so this doesn't happen again?' [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is using good, clear logic so important from the beginning to the end of your research?

options.A: It guarantees the hospital will fund the research project
options.B: It ensures conclusions directly match the gathered evidence
options.C: It removes the need for any statistical calculations
options.D: It stops patients from withdrawing from the study

explanation: Spot on! Sound logic stops us from making wild claims that our actual data doesn't back up. Keep it logical! [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is reflexivity important when analyzing qualitative data?

options.A: It speeds up the computer software processing time for transcripts
options.B: It helps researchers recognize and manage their personal biases
options.C: It automatically checks the mathematical accuracy of survey results
options.D: It proves that the study can be generalized to every hospital

explanation: Brilliant! Reflexivity means the researcher checks their own ego and personal views at the door so their own opinions don't colour the participants' stories. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why do nurses often prefer a syringe driver over intermittent injections in palliative care?

options.A: It works without requiring batteries or electrical power
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any nursing documentation
options.C: It allows family members to freely change drug doses at home
options.D: It avoids painful peaks and troughs by keeping drug levels steady

explanation: You got it! Continuous infusion stops drug levels from bouncing up and down, keeping pain and other symptoms nicely under control without roller-coaster effects. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is an important nursing duty after putting mydriatic eye drops in a patient's eyes for an exam?

options.A: Flush both eyes right away with normal saline
options.B: Keep them locked in a dark room for a whole day
options.C: Warn them about blurry vision and bright light sensitivity
options.D: Check their blood pressure every five minutes

explanation: Mydriatic drops widen the pupil and relax focusing muscles, making bright lights uncomfortable and vision blurry for a few hours. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which body is directly responsible for regulating nursing training and practice here in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
options.D: National Universities Commission

explanation: That's the NMCN! They are our main body, setting the rules and standards for all nursing schools and practice across the country. [learn more](GST322_U4_T10#GST322_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why do we consider pregnant teenagers and malnourished children as high-risk groups?

options.A: They have finished all required community health immunization schedules
options.B: They face a higher probability of poor health outcomes due to biological and social factors
options.C: They always live in urban hospital settings with easy access to doctors
options.D: They consume more public health resources than any other age group

explanation: Vulnerable groups often deal with a mix of body changes, growing needs, and tough living conditions. This makes it easier for them to fall sick, so nurses give them extra care and attention. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h1)

question: How do sensory areas and association areas work together?

options.A: Sensory areas control muscles while association areas block pain
options.B: Sensory areas register raw data while association areas give it meaning
options.C: Sensory areas interpret complex thoughts while association areas detect light
options.D: Sensory areas store memories while association areas process movement

explanation: The primary sensory cortex receives the basic sensation, and the adjacent association areas analyze and interpret what that sensation actually means. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T11#GNS211_U3_T11_h1)

question: What is the primary maternal health benefit of properly spacing pregnancies?

options.A: Permanently stopping all future menstrual cycles
options.B: Eliminating the need for any antenatal care visits
options.C: Giving the mother's body time to recover physically
options.D: Ensuring the mother gives birth only to male children

explanation: Proper spacing allows a woman's body to restore vital nutrients like iron and heal from the physical stress of a previous pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in nursing practice?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing medical supplies
options.B: To ensure injections do no harm to the patient or worker
options.C: To speed up the administration of routine vaccinations
options.D: To eliminate the need for personal protective equipment

explanation: Injection safety focuses entirely on protecting patients, healthcare workers, and the community from injury and disease transmission during injection procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T3#GNS122_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a clear example of using 'exclusion criteria'?

options.A: Leaving out patients who already have a severe kidney disease from a drug trial
options.B: Increasing the sample size after finding out the first group was too small
options.C: Admitting every patient who walks through the outpatient clinic door
options.D: Asking participants to write down their home addresses on a survey form

explanation: Exactly! Exclusion criteria help filter out people who might get harmed by the study or mess up the results. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h3)

question: Which harmless temporary side effect do many clients experience during their first few months on the pill?

options.A: Permanent hair loss
options.B: Breakthrough spotting
options.C: Loss of vision
options.D: Sudden bone fractures

explanation: Spotting between periods can be scary for clients, but reassure them it's very normal as the body adjusts to the new hormones in the first few months. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of establishing a clear case definition in surveillance?

options.A: Determining the exact cost of hospital treatment for insurance claims
options.B: Speeding up the time it takes to prescribe antibiotics to a patient
options.C: Fulfilling administrative paperwork requirements without clinical value
options.D: Ensuring everyone uses the exact same criteria to identify a disease

explanation: A standard case definition ensures that health workers across different regions are counting the exact same illness criteria. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T3#GNS313_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the traditional pillars of safe motherhood?

options.A: Antenatal care during pregnancy
options.B: Mandatory military service for parents
options.C: Family planning services
options.D: Postnatal care after delivery

explanation: Easy pick! Safe motherhood pillars focus on family planning, antenatal care, clean and safe delivery, and postnatal care—not military service! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h2)

question: What exactly is an 'out-of-pocket' payment in healthcare?

options.A: A monthly tax deducted automatically from a civil servant's salary
options.B: Direct cash paid by a patient to a provider at the time of service
options.C: Financial aid given by foreign countries to build clinics
options.D: A reimbursement paid by an insurance company to a hospital

explanation: An out-of-pocket payment is cash you bring straight from your purse or pocket to pay the hospital cash-and-carry style right when you get treated. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h2)

question: If both parents have the sickle cell trait (AS), what is the chance they will have a child with sickle cell anaemia (SS)?

options.A: 100 percent
options.B: 25 percent
options.C: 50 percent
options.D: 75 percent

explanation: Genetics can be tricky, but with AS carriers, there's a 1 in 4 (25%) chance per pregnancy of having an SS child. Knowing this helps us counsel families better! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is the final step in the core disease surveillance cycle?

options.A: Collecting more patient samples
options.B: Archiving reports in a cabinet
options.C: Destroying old laboratory records
options.D: Taking public health action

explanation: Data collection and analysis are useless unless they lead directly to meaningful public health action and control measures. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to create a private, non-judgmental space during patient counseling?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever contracting another infection
options.B: It eliminates the need to prescribe any pharmaceutical medications
options.C: It guarantees that the laboratory test results will return faster
options.D: It helps reduce fear of stigma so the patient shares accurate history

explanation: When patients feel safe and unjudged, they are much more likely to open up and tell you the truth about their health and partners. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is a major cause of family displacement and vulnerability across many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Conflict, banditry, and natural disasters
options.B: Mandatory retirement at age fifty
options.C: Too much funding from foreign donors
options.D: Government laws against farming

explanation: Correct! Insecurity and environmental challenges frequently displace Nigerian families, destroying their homes and traditional support systems. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T19#GNS225_U5_T19_h3)

question: What is a major worry when identical twins share a single placenta?

options.A: Guaranteed genetic difference in blood types
options.B: Permanent failure of maternal milk production
options.C: Complete absence of amniotic fluid in both sacs
options.D: Unequal blood sharing through connected blood vessels

explanation: Well done! Shared placentas often have shared blood vessels that can cause an imbalance in blood flow between the babies—something we watch out for as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h2)

question: Which imaging test is generally considered the best for viewing tissue death and fluid collections in acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Standard chest X-ray
options.B: Basic abdominal ultrasound
options.C: CT scan with contrast
options.D: Electrocardiogram strip

explanation: You got it! A contrast CT gives doctors the clearest pictures to spot inflammation, dead tissue, and hidden pockets of fluid around the pancreas. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which type of topical preparation is best for dry, thick, or scaly skin because it locks in moisture?

options.A: Lotion
options.B: Gel
options.C: Aqueous solution
options.D: Ointment

explanation: Ointments are oil-heavy, creating a protective blanket that stops moisture from escaping. Perfect for dry, scaly skin patches! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h2)

question: What should a nurse watch closest right after a patient gets an intracardiac injection?

options.A: Urine output using a bedside commode
options.B: Bowel sounds and abdominal softness
options.C: Cardiac rhythm and vital signs
options.D: Range of motion in the upper arms

explanation: You've got this! Because the heart muscle was just punctured, tracking heart rhythm and blood pressure helps catch dangerous complications right away. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T14#GNS125_U3_T14_h7)

question: Why might a client feel dizzy or shaky immediately after completing a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: The client has been deprived of clean drinking water for over 24 hours
options.B: A sudden surge of insulin can cause a temporary drop in blood sugar
options.C: Drawing multiple blood samples removes too many red blood cells
options.D: The concentrated sugar solution causes sudden dehydration of the brain

explanation: The large glucose load prompts an insulin spike that can overshoot and drop blood sugar below normal baseline levels, causing shakiness. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h7)

question: What is the main clinical reason for using the Z-track method during an IM injection?

options.A: To speed up the systemic absorption rate of local anesthetics
options.B: To prevent irritating medication from leaking into subcutaneous tissue
options.C: To eliminate the need for skin antisepsis before the procedure
options.D: To reduce the overall depth required for deep muscle penetration

explanation: Z-track is a smart trick! By pulling the skin sideways before sticking, you create a zigzag path that locks harsh or staining medicines deep in the muscle where they belong. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why do food safety officers frequently inspect local open-air markets and street food vendors?

options.A: These vendors feed a huge portion of the urban working-class population
options.B: Street vendors have more money to pay official fines
options.C: Open markets never have contamination problems
options.D: Large supermarkets are legally exempt from all safety checks

explanation: Since millions of people buy from local markets and street vendors every day, keeping those foods safe is crucial for public health. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T18#GNS214_U1_T18_h5)

question: What is a major advantage of providing home health care to new and expectant mothers?

options.A: It removes all financial costs associated with medical care.
options.B: It ensures the mother will have zero physical complications.
options.C: It allows nurses to observe the home environment and family support.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any future doctor visits.

explanation: Visiting the home gives nurses a clear picture of the patient's living conditions and support system, which directly impacts recovery and health. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h1)

question: What should a client do if she misses one combined pill by more than 12 hours?

options.A: Take three pills at once on the following morning
options.B: Take the missed pill right away and continue the rest as normal
options.C: Throw away the entire packet and wait for her next period
options.D: Stop taking birth control pills for the rest of that month

explanation: Don't panic over one missed pill! Just take the missed one immediately and keep going with the pack as usual. Protection is usually still intact. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T012#GNS226_U6_T012_h6)

question: What is the classic symptom reported by a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Inability to empty the bladder completely
options.B: Severe sharp pain during ovulation
options.C: Passage of gas or stool through the vagina
options.D: Continuous watery discharge from the urethra

explanation: Because of the abnormal opening, bowel contents escape through the vaginal canal instead of the anus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: Besides personal interest, what else does a researcher need for their chosen topic?

options.A: A personal relationship with the hospital director
options.B: A degree in computer engineering
options.C: Relevant clinical expertise and methodological skills
options.D: At least ten years of experience living abroad

explanation: You need to understand the clinical setting and know how to collect and look at your data properly to get trustworthy results. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h5)

question: Which specific blood cells are responsible for making antibodies when germs invade?

options.A: B-cells
options.B: T-cells
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Platelets

explanation: Great job! B-cells are our immune system's antibody factories, specially built to target foreign invaders. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h2)

question: When should discharge planning ideally start for a patient in subacute care?

options.A: After physical therapy finishes
options.B: Forty-eight hours before leaving
options.C: When the family requests it
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Spot on! Starting on day one ensures home changes, equipment, and family training are sorted out without last-minute rush. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h6)

question: Which vein inside the bend of the elbow (antecubital fossa) is usually our first choice for drawing blood?

options.A: Cephalic vein
options.B: Femoral vein
options.C: Median cubital vein
options.D: Basilic vein

explanation: The median cubital vein is your best friend in the ward! It sits nicely, doesn't roll around easily, and makes a great target for your needle. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which monitoring method provides the only true proof that sterilization successfully killed all bacterial spores?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape
options.B: Visual inspection for rust
options.C: Mechanical pressure gauges
options.D: Biological indicators

explanation: Biological indicators use actual heat-resistant bacterial spores to verify that the machine successfully destroyed all microbial life. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What is a major problem when writing infection control policies?

options.A: Making them too long and complicated for busy staff to use
options.B: Writing them in English instead of the local native language
options.C: Printing them on paper instead of viewing them on a mobile phone
options.D: Including pictures of medical equipment that look too modern

explanation: Exactly! If a policy is too heavy and academic, busy nurses on a tense shift won't have time to read it. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h4)

question: Why is it clinically important for nurses to separate biological sex from gender?

options.A: Gender is the only factor that matters for prescribing medications safely
options.B: Biological sex has no impact on a person's health outcomes whatsoever
options.C: Physical examinations are entirely unrelated to the concept of gender
options.D: Patients have both biological health needs and social experiences that affect care

explanation: Recognizing both biological and social dimensions ensures that nurses address the complete health profile of every patient without making false assumptions. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the best way for a nurse administrator to handle a valid complaint about poor hospital services?

options.A: Punish the patient for speaking out against the hospital management
options.B: Investigate the complaint fairly and put measures in place to fix the issue
options.C: Ignore the complaint completely so the issue disappears on its own
options.D: Blame junior nursing staff in public without checking the facts

explanation: Handling complaints openly builds trust! Investigating fairly helps fix underlying problems and shows patients that their voices matter. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h7)

question: Why is embedding midwives within local Nigerian communities so effective for maternal health?

options.A: It ensures that mothers never experience any pregnancy complications.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for primary health care centers.
options.C: It builds trust and helps overcome cultural and geographical barriers.
options.D: It allows midwives to practice without any formal government oversight.

explanation: When midwives live and work within the community, they break down distance and trust barriers that usually discourage women from seeking care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h1)

question: What factor has the greatest influence on peripheral vascular resistance?

options.A: Total vessel length
options.B: Overall body height
options.C: Vessel radius
options.D: Red blood cell count

explanation: Small changes in vessel radius create exponential changes in resistance, making constriction and dilation the primary way the body controls blood pressure. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why does putting in a urinary catheter raise a patient's risk of getting an infection?

options.A: It stops the kidneys from producing urine
options.B: It turns the skin into a non-living reservoir
options.C: It destroys all white blood cells in the bladder
options.D: It creates an artificial pathway for bacteria to enter

explanation: Spot on! Catheters bypass the body's natural defenses, giving bacteria a direct highway into the urinary tract. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why does a local skin infection or wound feel warm when you touch it?

options.A: Bacteria naturally generate a high amount of chemical heat
options.B: Increased blood flow brings extra warm blood to the area
options.C: Nerve endings fire rapidly and create friction warmth
options.D: Sweat glands lock up and trap body heat in the skin

explanation: Correct! Your body sends extra blood rushing to the infection site to bring helpful immune cells, which naturally makes the skin feel warm. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h3)

question: What does 'medicalisation of FGM' actually mean?

options.A: Using modern anesthesia during traditional cutting
options.B: Researching new surgical methods to reverse FGM
options.C: Treating the medical complications caused by FGM
options.D: FGM procedures being performed by healthcare workers

explanation: Medicalisation simply means when doctors, nurses, or other health workers are the ones performing the cutting. It's dangerous because it wrongly makes the practice look safe or acceptable. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why does the structural difference between gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria matter in pharmacology?

options.A: It dictates the correct storage temperature for oral medications
options.B: It determines how fast a patient's kidneys filter out IV fluids
options.C: It explains why certain bacterial types are harder to treat with specific drugs
options.D: It tells the nurse exactly how many calories the patient needs daily

explanation: Gram-negative bacteria have an extra protective outer membrane that blocks many standard antibiotics, requiring specific drug choices. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h7)

question: When you are caring for a very sick patient who cannot respond, what is your main job as their nurse?

options.A: Discharging the patient as quickly as possible
options.B: Focusing solely on medication administration schedules
options.C: Waiting for family members to make all clinical decisions
options.D: Acting as the patient's primary defense and surrogate voice

explanation: You've got this! Since very ill patients can't speak up for themselves, you become their voice and protector to make sure they get safe, complete care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main goal of genetic counseling for couples in communities with high sickle cell rates?

options.A: To test newborns for immediate signs of acute chest syndrome
options.B: To provide accurate information on inheritance risks for family planning
options.C: To administer prophylactic antibiotics to prevent bacterial infections
options.D: To prescribe daily doses of folic acid for blood cell production

explanation: Counseling empowers couples with clear facts about their genotypes so they can make informed, confident family planning choices. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h6)

question: A patient with chest pain is awake and chatting with you in the clinic. Why should you NOT put an AED on them?

options.A: Chest pain medication must be given before applying any emergency electronic device.
options.B: The device only delivers shocks to patients who are unresponsive and in cardiac arrest.
options.C: The AED will automatically call emergency services if turned on near a living person.
options.D: The AED battery will drain too quickly if used on a conscious patient.

explanation: AEDs are smart! They check the heart rhythm and will only give a shock if a dangerous, shockable rhythm is found. If a patient is awake and breathing, the AED won't do anything—and they don't need one. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T13#GNS212_U4_T13_h1)

question: A village has no local markets, poor farming land, and high unemployment. What health issue is most likely to spike here?

options.A: Stress-related injuries from high-speed driving
options.B: Malnutrition and poverty-related illnesses
options.C: Occupational hazards from heavy factory work
options.D: Complications from cosmetic plastic surgeries

explanation: Exactly. When the local economy struggles and people can't get basic food or income, malnutrition and poverty-related health issues naturally follow. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h2)

question: A colleague asks to quickly log in under your computer account because they forgot their password. What should you do?

options.A: Complete the charting for them under your own name instead
options.B: Refuse and ask them to log in using their own credentials
options.C: Allow them to type quickly while you watch over their shoulder
options.D: Write your password down on a sticky note for them to use later

explanation: Always keep your login secure! Sharing it means you take the blame for whatever gets charted on that account. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h8)

question: Which body posture helps open up the spaces between the vertebrae for a spinal tap?

options.A: Arching the back backward with arms extended
options.B: Lying completely flat on the back with straight legs
options.C: Sitting upright with shoulders pulled straight back
options.D: Curled up with knees and chin tucked inward

explanation: Spot on! Flexing the spine forward separates the bones, widening the gap so the needle can pass through easily. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T9#GNS221_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why do blood collection sample tubes come with different colored tops?

options.A: They contain different chemical additives for specific tests
options.B: They indicate the date the tubes were manufactured
options.C: They show which department ordered the laboratory test
options.D: They represent the different sizes of the patient's veins

explanation: Those color codes are lifesavers! They tell you which additive (like anticoagulants or clot activators) is inside for specific lab investigations. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h4)

question: In Nigerian reproductive health programs, what does the acronym PMTCT stand for?

options.A: Primary Medical Treatment for Chronic Tumors
options.B: Prevention of Mother-To-Child Transmission
options.C: Public Midwifery Training and Community Testing
options.D: Postnatal Management of Teenage Children and Teens

explanation: You got it! PMTCT programs focus on stopping HIV from passing from an infected mother to her baby during pregnancy, birth, or breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why must public health measures continue even if a disease is wiped out in Nigeria?

options.A: Local health workers lose their medical licenses after an outbreak
options.B: The pathogen can still be imported from other regions where it exists
options.C: Patients will develop allergies if vaccination programs stop
options.D: Eliminated diseases always mutate into completely different organisms

explanation: As long as the germ is active in other parts of the world, travelers or animals can easily bring it back across borders. Stay alert! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of reproductive coercion in a relationship?

options.A: Promoting healthy spacing between all children in a community
options.B: Ensuring family planning clinics are adequately funded
options.C: Reducing overall maternal mortality rates in rural hospitals
options.D: Controlling a partner's reproductive outcomes to maintain power

explanation: Well done! Reproductive coercion involves tactics like tampering with birth control to force or block a pregnancy, keeping the victim trapped and dependent. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T10#GNS312_U4_T10_h5)

question: Which hormone gets released when fats and proteins show up in the small intestine?

options.A: Cholecystokinin
options.B: Aldosterone
options.C: Erythropoietin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Cholecystokinin (let's just call it CCK!) is the hormone that shouts to the gallbladder and pancreas: 'Hey, fatty food has arrived, time to release your juices!' [learn more](GNS121_U1_T5#GNS121_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when monitoring a client's nutritional progress?

options.A: Checking regular weight trends over time
options.B: Ignoring client feedback on food preferences
options.C: Documenting specific physical measurements
options.D: Reviewing the client's recent food diaries

explanation: Never ignore what the client likes! Diet plans only work if they fit the client's personal lifestyle and taste. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h7)

question: Which sign around a skull pin site should ring alarm bells and be reported immediately?

options.A: A small amount of clear dried crusting
options.B: Mild redness that disappears within a day
options.C: Purulent yellow drainage and a foul odor
options.D: Normal skin color around the metal screw

explanation: Pus and bad smells always point to an infection setting in. Let the doctor know right away so it can be treated! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h6)

question: How does severe income inequality affect the overall health of a population?

options.A: It eliminates chronic stress among lower-income earners.
options.B: It completely stops the spread of infectious diseases.
options.C: It places a heavy disease burden on poorer groups who cannot afford early care.
options.D: It ensures that everyone has equal access to private clinics.

explanation: Wide gaps in wealth mean poorer citizens cannot afford preventive care or early treatment, allowing minor sicknesses to develop into severe, chronic illnesses. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is a classic warning sign that a patient might have pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.A: Painful ulcers forming inside the oral cavity
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the sclera and skin
options.C: Sudden swelling of the lower extremities
options.D: A persistent cough lasting more than two weeks

explanation: That's right! Whenever a patient walks in with a cough that just won't quit for over two weeks, TB should immediately pop into your nursing mind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h3)

question: Which classroom setup helps prevent you from feeling sleepy during long lectures?

options.A: Bright neon paint and loud music
options.B: Proper lighting and good ventilation
options.C: Complete darkness with shut windows
options.D: Tight, cramped seating to save space

explanation: Fresh air and good lighting keep headaches and sleepiness away, helping you stay sharp and focused while your lecturer is talking. [learn more](GST321_U8_T3#GST321_U8_T3_h2)

question: A patient with severe burn wounds is at risk of poor healing if which nutritional goal is missed?

options.A: Meeting their increased energy expenditure needs
options.B: Eliminating all dietary fats from their meals
options.C: Reducing their daily protein consumption
options.D: Restricting their fluid intake to prevent swelling

explanation: Brilliant! Burn patients undergo massive stress and need plenty of calories and protein. If we don't meet their soaring energy needs, their tissues simply won't heal properly. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h7)

question: What is the main job of a second-order neuron in a sensory pathway?

options.A: Carrying the signal from the spinal cord or brainstem up to the thalamus
options.B: Detecting the initial environmental stimulus at the skin receptor
options.C: Sending final motor output directly to the skeletal muscle
options.D: Producing neurotransmitters inside the primary motor cortex

explanation: Think of second-order neurons as the middle relay runners, taking the sensory baton from the spinal cord and passing it all the way up to the thalamus. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T16#GNS211_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which two nutrients are most essential for building and maintaining strong bones?

options.A: Iron and vitamin B12
options.B: Potassium and sodium
options.C: Protein and vitamin C
options.D: Calcium and vitamin D

explanation: Calcium builds bone structure, and vitamin D is necessary for the body to absorb that calcium properly. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T25#GNS222_U1_T25_h5)

question: How many sections make up the abdominopelvic quadrant system?
explanation: The abdominopelvic area is split into four quadrants for rapid clinical screening during assessments. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the absolute best way to check if a patient is ready to give their own shots at home?

options.A: Ask a family member to take full responsibility for the task
options.B: Provide a written multiple-choice test on injection theory
options.C: Have the patient perform a return demonstration of the steps
options.D: Ask the patient to read the medication package insert aloud

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them show you how they do it lets you coach them, build their confidence, and make sure they are doing it safely. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h7)

question: When is it safe to upgrade a patient from clear fluids to full fluids?

options.A: Immediately upon admission before any assessment occurs
options.B: When the patient demands solid meat and fibrous vegetables
options.C: When the patient tolerates clear fluids without nausea or cramping
options.D: When the patient develops severe diarrhea from dairy products

explanation: We step things up gradually. If their tummy handles clear fluids well without vomiting or cramps, they are ready for the next level! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h3)

question: A nurse is getting ready to clean a blood pressure cuff used on a patient with unbroken skin. What level of cleaning is enough?

options.A: Absolute sterilization
options.B: High-level disinfection
options.C: Sporicidal treatment
options.D: Low-level disinfection

explanation: Since a BP cuff only touches intact skin, it is a non-critical item. A simple low-level disinfection gets the job done! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is the biggest risk of waiting too long to report a sudden drop in a patient's neuro status?

options.A: It increases the financial cost of hospital room supplies
options.B: It causes the nursing documentation to look untidy
options.C: It can delay life-saving interventions for acute brain injury
options.D: It forces the patient to stay in the hospital an extra day

explanation: Brain emergencies move fast! Reporting changes immediately can be the difference between a full recovery and permanent damage. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h9)

question: Which hormone do standard pregnancy test strips detect to confirm that implantation has happened?

options.A: Follicle-stimulating hormone
options.B: Basal testosterone
options.C: Luteinizing hormone
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: You nailed it! hCG is produced by the newly implanted cells and shows up in blood and urine, making it the classic marker on pregnancy tests. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h5)

question: A nurse leading a polio vaccination campaign notices sudden community resistance due to false rumors spread on social media. What is the best immediate response?

options.A: Punish any community member who asks questions about the vaccine
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders to openly address and debunk the rumors
options.C: Ignore the rumors completely and hope the villagers forget them
options.D: Cancel the entire vaccination campaign and close the health clinic

explanation: Rumors spread fast, but trusted local voices spread clarity faster! Partnering with community leaders is the best way to calm fears and protect public health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h8)

question: When we talk about the 'virulence' of a germ, what do we mean?

options.A: The ability of the organism to simply enter and multiply inside a human host
options.B: The total number of people who have been exposed to the microorganism
options.C: The speed at which the pathogen can travel through the open air
options.D: The severity of the disease and the likelihood of causing severe illness or death

explanation: Virulence is basically how fierce or damaging the germ is. A highly virulent germ packs a really heavy punch! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T78#GNS214_U1_T78_h4)

question: What triggers the sudden rush of milk right after childbirth?

options.A: An immediate rise in maternal body temperature
options.B: The sudden drop in estrogen and progesterone levels
options.C: The total disappearance of prolactin from the blood
options.D: A massive spike in placental hormone production

explanation: Exactly! Once the placenta is delivered, those blocking hormones plummet, allowing prolactin to finally do its job and bring in the milk. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h2)

question: Why is Post-Abortion Care (PAC) considered a complete, all-round care model?

options.A: It involves police reports for every single case
options.B: It delays discharge until lab results are ready
options.C: It combines emergency treatment, family planning, and emotional support
options.D: It focuses only on theatre surgeries

explanation: PAC looks at the whole patient—healing her body, supporting her emotions, and helping her plan for the future. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T008#GNS226_U5_T008_h6)

question: How do standard antacids give quick relief from heartburn and ulcers?

options.A: Chemically neutralizing existing acid in the stomach
options.B: Creating a physical barrier over the ulcer crater
options.C: Killing the bacteria that cause stomach ulcers
options.D: Stopping parietal cells from manufacturing new acid

explanation: Antacids act like a chemical sponge, directly neutralizing the acid that is already sitting in the stomach and causing that burning feeling. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h4)

question: What type of data is mostly used in explanatory research designs?

options.A: Numerical measurements and statistical testing
options.B: Only handwritten personal diaries from patients
options.C: Random historical fiction books
options.D: Unstructured gossip from hospital hallways

explanation: Well done! Explanatory designs use numbers and statistics to clearly show cause-and-effect links. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T13#GNS224_U1_T13_h3)

question: Besides eating healthy food, what is the big benefit of practicing portion control?

options.A: Maintaining energy balance and preventing excessive weight gain
options.B: Ensuring that digestion takes place only during nighttime hours
options.C: Eliminating the need to consume any carbohydrates at all
options.D: Reducing the body's overall requirement for clean drinking water

explanation: Exactly. Portion control stops us from taking in more energy than we burn off, helping us stay at a healthy weight. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h5)

question: A patient with Parkinson's disease is at high risk for falls. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Implement a comprehensive fall prevention plan and clear walking paths
options.B: Keep the patient strictly confined to bedrest at all times
options.C: Remove all supportive walking aids to force independent balance
options.D: Encourage the patient to run down hospital hallways for exercise

explanation: Stiffness and a shuffling gait mean falls are a real danger. Keeping pathways clear and taking smart safety precautions helps protect your patient while keeping them mobile. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T12#GNS211_U3_T12_h6)

question: A nurse wants to know a patient's actual food intake over the past day. Which assessment method is best suited for this?

options.A: A 24-hour dietary recall
options.B: An inpatient surgical biopsy
options.C: A two-week physical exercise log
options.D: A complete genetic blood screening

question: Which of these is NOT a good nursing strategy for helping a patient manage multiple medications?

options.A: Encouraging the use of weekly pillboxes or organizers to track daily doses
options.B: Educating the patient on recognizing early warning signs of adverse drug reactions
options.C: Collaborating with the pharmacist to simplify complicated dosing schedules
options.D: Telling the patient to stop all their medications immediately without consulting the doctor

explanation: Never tell a patient to drop all meds at once! Stopping drugs abruptly can cause dangerous withdrawal or rebound health issues. Changes must always be planned. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h5)

question: Why would a nurse researcher choose a retrospective study to look into a very rare disease?

options.A: It costs nothing to access and analyze hospital databases
options.B: It proves the exact cause of the disease without any doubt
options.C: Past records already contain enough accumulated cases to study
options.D: Patients prefer answering questions about their past illnesses

explanation: Spot on! Because rare conditions take forever to pop up in real-time studies, looking backward at existing hospital records lets researchers gather enough cases right away. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T14#GNS224_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why do endocrine disorders often cause symptoms all over the body in different organs?

options.A: Endocrine glands are physically connected to every single organ in the human body
options.B: Hormones travel systemically through the bloodstream to reach many different target tissues
options.C: The liver automatically spreads hormone imbalances to the digestive tract
options.D: Hormone receptors are identical across all types of tissues and organs

explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers that travel far and wide through the bloodstream. If there's too much or too little of one, every organ that has receptors for it will feel the impact! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T13#GNS222_U2_T13_h8)

question: Why is it so important to ask about a client's last menstrual period before starting birth control?

options.A: To check if the client has an active sexually transmitted infection

options.C: To reasonably rule out an existing, early pregnancy before starting birth control
options.D: To determine how many children the client has delivered in the past

question: What major nutrition paradox do we see in many societies today?

options.C: Everyone in the world now has access to too much food
options.D: People no longer eat carbohydrates or fats anywhere

question: What does angiotensin II normally do to your blood vessels?

options.A: Widens the blood vessels
options.B: Destroys blood platelets
options.C: Relaxes the vessel walls
options.D: Narrows the blood vessels

explanation: Angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor—it squeezes your blood vessels tight to quickly push your blood pressure back up. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h4)

question: When does most of the myelination (insulation) happen in the human nervous system?

options.A: Only after a person reaches full physical adulthood
options.B: Immediately before the neural tube closes
options.C: Starting late in fetal development and continuing into adolescence
options.D: Exclusively during the first three weeks of embryonic life

explanation: Exactly! Myelination starts before birth for basic tasks, but it keeps going all through childhood and into our teenage years. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h6)

question: What does it usually mean if a baby's weight line drops downwards across percentiles on a growth chart?

options.A: Rapid acceleration of normal muscle mass
options.B: A normal growth spurt following a brief illness
options.C: Potential nutritional deficit or underlying health problem
options.D: An error in the initial recording of the birth weight

explanation: Spot on! A downward drop in weight percentiles is a warning sign that the baby might be falling behind due to illness or poor feeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h5)

question: What technology does flow cytometry use to help diagnose conditions like leukaemia?

options.A: Cell surface markers
options.B: X-ray beams
options.C: Electrical heart signals
options.D: Urine dipsticks

explanation: Flow cytometry uses special tags to spot unique proteins on the outside of abnormal blood cells, helping doctors pinpoint the exact issue. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h6)

question: How often should you reposition an immobile neurological patient to protect their skin?

options.A: Only when requested
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Every six hours

explanation: Turning patients every two hours takes the pressure off bony areas, which is one of the best ways to stop pressure sores from forming. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T24#GNS222_U3_T24_h4)

question: Why are midwives in remote Nigerian health clinics allowed to give certain emergency drugs on their own?

options.A: Doctors are often unavailable during urgent obstetric situations
options.B: Standard hospital policy prohibits doctors from prescribing to newborns
options.C: Midwives complete more medical pharmacology training than doctors
options.D: Pharmacies are legally banned from stocking maternal medications

explanation: You've got this! In remote areas where a doctor might not be around, midwives need the power to act fast and save lives. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h1)

question: Which bacteria is well-known for causing rapid and severe postpartum infections?

options.A: Group A Streptococcus
options.B: Candida albicans
options.C: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.D: Corynebacterium diphtheriae

explanation: Group A Streptococcus is notorious in midwifery for causing very rapid and severe illness in new mothers. Quick action is always key here! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T024#GNS226_U3_T024_h2)

question: In the formula for a t-statistic, what does the top number (numerator) show?

options.A: The difference between the two group averages
options.B: The predetermined p-value threshold
options.C: The total number of participants in the study
options.D: The standard error or internal variation

question: Which of these is a classic example of a primary source in nursing research?

options.A: A systematic review article written by an outside professor
options.B: A newspaper editorial commenting on a new health policy
options.C: A textbook chapter summarizing ten different research articles
options.D: An original research report written by the scientists who did the study

explanation: Primary sources are direct, firsthand accounts written straight by the actual researchers who performed the study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h3)

question: An elderly client is returning home after hip surgery. What is the best safety upgrade to make in their bathroom?

options.A: Placing a thick cloth rug directly on the slippery wet floor
options.B: Installing grab bars near the toilet and inside the shower
options.C: Removing the bathroom door to allow faster nursing access
options.D: Turning off bathroom lights at night to encourage rest

question: Besides movement, what other important job do joints do for the body?

options.A: Regulating body temperature
options.B: Producing red blood cells
options.C: Maintaining posture and skeletal alignment
options.D: Filtering waste products from the blood

explanation: Great job! Joints work hand-in-hand with your muscles to hold your skeleton upright and keep your posture steady. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T7#GNS121_U3_T7_h6)

question: A patient admits to regularly eating undercooked pork. Which type of worm infection are they most at risk for?

options.B: Pinworm infestation
options.C: Tapeworm infection
options.D: Schistosomiasis

question: Where does the reservoir fit in the chain of infection?

options.A: It provides the home and starting point for the infectious germ
options.B: It acts as the final portal of entry into the new host
options.C: It functions as the chemical agent used to sterilize instruments
options.D: It serves as the physical method of airborne transmission

explanation: The reservoir is always link number one—it's the cozy starting home where the germ hangs out before starting its journey. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h3)

question: A nurse manager wants a new pressure sore prevention check to stick. What is the most effective strategy?

options.A: Keep the new check a secret until the end of the year evaluation
options.B: Add the check directly into the routine vital sign documentation round
options.C: Require nurses to write a separate essay report every single morning
options.D: Punish any nurse who forgets to mention the project in weekly meetings

explanation: Aligning new tasks with existing routines prevents them from feeling like burdensome extra chores. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is accurate home care documentation especially critical compared to hospital notes?

options.A: Hospital records are destroyed as soon as the patient is discharged.
options.B: Insurance companies never read hospital charts, only home visit notes.
options.C: Home patients are legally required to keep a copy of every nurse's note.
options.D: Home nurses work independently and their notes are the main record of care.

explanation: Spot on! Since home nurses work on their own without a team standing right beside them, detailed notes are vital for tracking progress safely. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h7)

question: What quick bedside test helps confirm if a skin rash is caused by a fungus?

options.A: Gram stain of blood cultures
options.B: Complete blood cell count
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Potassium hydroxide (KOH) wet mount

question: Why are home modifications like building ramps and widening doors often a major financial challenge?

options.A: Assistive devices mean you never need home alterations
options.B: Building codes make structural changes illegal
options.C: They require specialized labor and materials that insurance rarely covers
options.D: Modified homes cause higher utility bills

explanation: Renovating a house to make it wheelchair-accessible takes cash upfront. Because health insurance in our setting rarely covers home repairs, families carry the burden alone. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h3)

question: What should a nursing lecturer do first before using any instructional media in class?

options.A: Preview and test the material beforehand
options.B: Ask students to pay for the equipment
options.C: Hand out a surprise test on the topic
options.D: Turn off all lights in the classroom

explanation: Testing equipment and reviewing materials ahead of time prevents technical hitdrops and ensures smooth lesson delivery. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h5)

question: A patient knows her diet is unhealthy and plans to start eating vegetables next week, but hasn't bought any yet. Which stage is she in?

options.A: Precontemplation
options.B: Preparation
options.C: Maintenance
options.D: Action

explanation: She is getting ready to make a change very soon (like planning for next week), which puts her right in the preparation stage. You've got this! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h2)

question: What is the main goal of system reliability in healthcare?

options.A: How consistently a clinical process produces safe outcomes
options.B: The total number of disciplinary actions taken against staff
options.C: How many patients a single nurse can care for in a shift
options.D: The speed at which doctors answer emergency calls

explanation: You've got this! System reliability simply means how dependably a process delivers safe, correct results every single time. [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h1)

question: How do patient satisfaction surveys help a home health agency improve its care?

options.A: By serving as legal proof that no errors ever occurred in the home
options.B: By replacing all internal clinical audits and staff evaluations
options.C: By identifying operational weaknesses and areas needing service adjustment
options.D: By reducing the total number of patients assigned to each nurse

explanation: Listening directly to client feedback gives agencies clear insight into what's working and where care can be made even better. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T7#GNS324_U2_T7_h6)

question: What exactly is salpingitis?

options.B: Malignant growth inside the uterine muscle wall
options.C: Fungal overgrowth within the vaginal vault
options.D: Infection and inflammation of the fallopian tubes

question: Why is being an advocate so important for a community health nurse?

options.B: Doctors refuse to speak with families directly

question: What is a great way to encourage nurses to speak up and report clinical errors or near-misses?

options.C: Fostering a supportive, non-punitive reporting culture
options.D: Firing any nurse who makes a minor documentation mistake

question: A patient develops a severe fear of water after nearly drowning as a child. What caused this phobia?

options.A: Genetic inheritance
options.B: Observational learning
options.C: Traumatic direct experience
options.D: Information transmission

question: Where should community-based mental health interventions ideally take place to be most effective?

question: Which of these is NOT a normal job of a healthy kidney?

options.D: Clearing parathyroid hormone from the blood

question: Which major body cavity contains both the heart and the lungs?

question: During early blood loss, what is the body's main goal to protect itself?

options.C: Maintain blood supply to the brain and heart
options.D: Keep the skin warm and well-perfused

question: A nursing student is counseling a new mother who fears that modern contraceptives cause permanent infertility. How should the student respond?
